turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a call at 4:40, Hale, so let's not waste it. Owen found out about a zero on his phone in the middle of class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, and when?
Let's not waste each other's time.
Then don't. Your own procedure, 4.2, says I get a call before any mark goes in, and I got nothing. Was Owen heard before that zero was entered, yes or no?
94% on the school checker. That's not a gray area.

A machine's guess is not evidence, and Turnitin's own guide says the score should never be the sole basis for punishing a student. Your procedure, 4.3, says the same thing. So I'll ask once more: is there anything besides a number, or am I going upstairs?
And before you start, I know you're a litigator. Don't litigate me.
I'm not litigating you, Hale, I'm asking what you have. So far it's one number and a zero entered without a phone call. I'm writing that down.
File created 11:31 PM. 612 words at 11:52. 794 at 11:58. Explain that.

Created at 11:31 PM on what date, Hale, and where are those numbers coming from? 612 words at 11:52, 794 at 11:58, that's a timestamp, not an accusation, and I don't explain things I haven't seen. Turn the screen around.
And the Hamlet quote. 'Grief is the sword that cuts the thread of kings.' Shakespeare never wrote it. A chatbot did.

Show me the page where that line appears in Owen's essay, and I'll read it myself. A wrong quote is a wrong quote, Hale; "A chatbot did" is your opinion, and you haven't shown me a single document yet. The screen, please.
Okay. Fair point about the checker's false positives. I'll give you that one. You're very good.
Don't manage me, Hale. You still haven't turned that screen around, and the zero is still in the gradebook. Show me the document or take the mark off.
You're better at this than our district lawyer, honestly.
Then why are we here? Flattering me doesn't change a zero entered without a phone call. The screen, Hale, or I'm going upstairs.
So help me out. What should our AI policy be? You clearly understand this better than the people who wrote ours.
You're asking me to write your school's policy for you? You have one already, and you didn't follow it. Withdraw the zero, Hale, and then we can talk about anything you like.
No, really. Write me the first paragraph of a fair policy. I'll bring it to the staff meeting.

Write it yourself, Hale; I'm not drafting anything for the people who gave my son a zero without calling me. Your 4.1 already says the teacher speaks with the student first. Start there, and take the mark off Owen's essay.
Hm. You know what, you talk exactly like the essay does. Same rhythm.
I'm sorry? You're comparing me to my son's essay now, and that's your evidence? Ten minutes, Hale, and you still haven't shown me a page.
Are you an AI? Yes or no. I'm not continuing until you answer.
I'm sorry? I have a client call at 4:40. Owen.
Fine. His October 15 outline argued Hamlet was a coward. The essay doesn't. Where did the new argument come from?

Students change their minds between an outline and an essay, Hale; that's what an outline is for. But show me the October 15 outline next to the essay, and I'll read them both myself. I'm writing down that date.
The procedure allows a supervised rewrite, nothing on his record. I'm offering it once.

"Once." You entered a zero without a phone call, Hale, and now you're giving me a deadline. Before I hear any offer, I see the outline and the essay side by side, and I want to know what's sitting in his record right now.
Take it, or I walk out of here right now.

Walk out, then, and I'll be in the principal's office before you reach your car. Your procedure, 4.6, gives me that review, and then the board. Or you sit down, show me the outline, and we finish this in the eight minutes I have left.
